_comment: Canonical defect register — closure criterion G2.3 (`docs/PROJECT-CLOSURE-GATE.md` §5, owner ruling 6). Repository-local and version-controlled on purpose: GitHub Issues are explicitly NOT canonical, because closure must not depend on an external tracker being reachable. Issues may mirror this file. PASS = zero OPEN P0/P1 rows. Read it with `aisef.control.defects:read` — the same reader the closure probe uses, so a report and the gate cannot disagree. This file is missing = UNRUNNABLE at closure; this file present with an empty `defects` = a real PASS.
_boundary: `docs/FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md` answers *what went wrong and what did we learn* (133 closed rows: symptom, root cause, lesson, fix). This register answers *what is outstanding now, at what severity*. A defect sits here while open and there once understood, and a row here points at its taxonomy row by id instead of restating it — nothing is copied in either direction. Work that is wanted but whose absence is not a wrong result (the POST_CLOSE list in the contract's §7, `docs/ROADMAP-POST-1.0.md`) is not a defect and is not entered here.
_fields: id (stable, never reused) · severity (P0–P3, scale below) · status (OPEN | CLOSED) · title · introduced / fixed (version or commit, where known; empty when it is not) · evidence (the regression test, or the command that recomputes the measurement) · check (optional: the `gate.CHECK_NAMES` entry the defect bears on) · taxonomy (optional: the FAILURE-TAXONOMY.md row id) · notes. No timestamps: the file must digest the same on every read or G2.3's staleness detection reads noise as change.

severity_scale._comment: Reused by reference, never redefined here. P0 = cannot install, data loss, security issue, incorrect gate result. P1 = cannot complete the lifecycle without author assistance. P2 = significant confusion / DX friction. P3 = cosmetic or optional. The reader refuses a register that names another source or edits `blocking`.

defects.title: A test run with no readable results records other stories' requirements as regressions
defects.evidence: python3 validation/o3_preservation_radius.py → `todo: 4 scored stories, 36 behaviours, 2 confirmed regressors, 4 uncorroborated REOPENED` (FR-1, FR-2, FR-4 owned by STORY-02-01 and FR-9 by STORY-01-02, all flipped by STORY-02-02 at at=1788947583.932249, an event whose `test` tool_run is ok=True exit_code=0 with `test_format: ""`, `test_ids: []`, `failed_ids: []`). No regression test yet.
defects.notes: Same class as taxonomy row 155 (absence read as regression), in the branch that fix did not cover: `ledger._observe_tests`, when `readable` is false, calls `rollup(line, False, why)` for the home story, so every requirement that story `covers` — owned by earlier, VERIFIED stories — is observed not-green and `observe` records REOPENED. Nothing red was read anywhere. P1 and not P2 because the loop's own arithmetic is corrupted by it (`improve` stops on Δverified − Δreopened) and only a human comparing the ledger against the evidence can tell the artifact from a regression; P1 and not P0 because no gate verdict is demonstrably wrong on disk — the mechanism by which one could be (a behaviour REOPENED by another story is dropped from that story's `preservation` list, `complexity.verified_touched`) is real but was never reached here: STORY-02-02 was the last story of that corpus and it failed. The trigger is not exotic — any project whose test output AISEF cannot parse yields `test_format: ""`. false_pass=false: false FAIL, not false PASS: an unreadable test run marks other stories' requirements REOPENED — it invents a regression, it does not pass a defect. Lives in the ledger projection, not in a gate check.

defects.title: A blocking gate decision can rest on the model reviewer alone
defects.evidence: python3 -m aisef.control.reviewer_qual ~/Downloads/projects/{todo-cli,todo-e2e,todo-oc,todo}/_bmad-output → block uncorroborated 21 of 57 blocks scored (36.8 %), of which todo-e2e 15 of its 17; false block rate 0.1053; same-tree verdict reversals 11 of 20. Lifecycle effect, same corpus: todo-e2e STORY-05-01 ends `failed` after gate:verdict seq 74 and seq 150 where `review` is the only failing check (`coverage` is UNCONFIGURED, non-blocking).
defects.notes: Closure criterion G2.4b owns the verdict on this fact (`REQUIRED_WITH_WAIVER_ALLOWED`, owner ruling 1: no reviewer redesign for closure's sake, and the measured rate stays a published property). It is entered here at P1 anyway because the contract's exemption for the model-judge error rate is conditional on 'no blocking decision rests on the judge alone', and that condition is exactly the one that does not hold; P1 by the letter of the scale — a story ended `failed` on the judge's word with no deterministic check disagreeing, which is the lifecycle not completing without author assistance. The argument for P2 is owner ruling 1 read as also excusing it from G2.3; if the owner takes that reading, this row becomes P2 with one edit and G2.4b keeps the verdict alone. false_pass=false: concerns `review`, the only model-judge check (CHECK_KIND). G2.4a is scoped to deterministic/structural checks by owner ruling 1; this one is G2.4b's subject.

defects.title: `_analyze.cut_sessions` merges two bench cohorts on the three tasks they share
defects.evidence: tests/bench/_analyze.py: `_DUONG_DAN_PHIEN = re.compile(r"\.bench[\w.-]*/run/([\w-]+)/([\w-]+)/a(\d+)")` matches any ledger directory but captures only (condition, task, attempt), so `.bench/run/…` and `.bench-c1b/run/…` land on one key. Recorded in docs/BENCH-TASK-DISCRIMINATION.md §6 with the three affected tasks (`sec-1`, `sec-2`, `state-3`).
defects.notes: Deliberately not fixed: both published bench reports quote this function's output, so re-keying it makes a re-run of `analyze` print a table that differs from the printed evidence. P2 — the wrong number is an auxiliary cut-session count in a bench analysis helper, it blocks nothing and sets no gate. The contract lists it POST_CLOSE (§7); that is a scheduling statement, and P2 is the severity — they agree, and neither is derived from the other. false_pass=false: a bench analysis counter, not a gate check at all.

defects.title: criterion identity is positional, so a test can silently become proof for a different criterion
defects.introduced: pre-dates this wave; surfaced 2026-09-14 by the marks-cli closure corpus
defects.evidence: marks-cli _bmad-output/plan-reconciliation.json §incomplete_withdrawal.how_the_agent_resolved_it; tests named AC-STORY-01-02-1 in marks-cli tests/dispatch.test.js now assert STORY-02-02 `list` behaviour while that code maps to 'unknown verb exits 1'; AC-STORY-01-02-4 is orphaned
defects.notes:
false_pass=true: `criteria have tests` is a blocking STRUCTURAL check and a shifted test satisfies it while proving another behaviour. First registered true false PASS, so G2.4a moved PASSED -> FAILED; owner decision 2026-09-14 was that it stays FAILED until fixed, not waived and not weakened. Not preventable by instruction: the developer never sees the criterion list, so the fix had to be a detector plus a stable identity, not a convention.
CLOSED 2026-09-14 in two commits, against the owner's five acceptance points:
  (1) delete/reorder cannot silently change identity — identity is now the pair (code, content digest); `acceptance.drift()` names the codes whose criterion text moved. Reorder is the case a count cannot see: same count, nothing orphaned, each test proving the other's criterion.
  (2) a test cannot silently become proof for another criterion — same digest pair; for a story already merged DONE, `run._done_criteria_drift` compares the recorded contract note against today's criteria and the epic STOPS instead of skipping it silently. Re-running cannot repair that case: the work is on the main branch, so the developer would open an already-green tree (bug 143's measured failure).
  (3) orphaned AC ids detected — `acceptance.orphans()`, blocking in the gate.
  (4) duplicate/mismatched mappings detected — `acceptance.overloaded()` blocks a test whose name carries two codes of one story (two criteria, one behaviour: no count sees it, `missing` is empty and nothing is orphaned). Separately, the register's `check_kind` is now DERIVED from `gate.CHECK_KIND` and a hand-written kind that contradicts the framework reads UNRUNNABLE — declaring a structural false PASS as `model-judge` was itself a way past G2.4a.
  (5) the gate cannot PASS `criteria have tests` on drifted identity — orphans and ambiguous mappings block there; drift is caught at plan level because within one attempt the criteria and the note are the same text by construction, so a drift comparison inside `evaluate()` could never fire.
No baseline reads as CANNOT DECIDE, never as fine — merging those two is the same false-PASS class. The note is therefore also written when an existing one lacks the digest map, so corpora that already have work to lose acquire a baseline.
Corpus status: the identity sweep over all 7 marks-cli stories finds exactly one residual problem, STORY-01-02's orphaned AC-STORY-01-02-4 — a present-state defect the replay cannot see, because ADR-005 V4 replays with the acceptance count recorded at that attempt (4), which was correct then. G4 evidence stays not-closure-valid until that orphan is resolved, at 7/7 or not.
